title: Program Kit canonical public-analyzer release binding and reproducible packages
intent: Make every published public generated-source analyzer selection discoverable from the installed CLI, bind that selection to immutable NuGet.org repository-signed bytes and exact generated-output generator revisions, execution-link those revisions through generated-output evidence, and produce the coordinated alpha.3 unsigned candidate closure reproducibly through repository-owned package canonicalization before a human-started workflow finalizes published evidence.
scope: Stable private and public compiler participation receipts that do not change compiled outputs.
Explicit source-root normalization and deterministic Program Kit assembly production.
Repository-owned deterministic canonicalization of every manifest-selected unsigned nupkg, including the consumer meta-package.
Explicit candidate-package, package-content, and NuGet.org repository-signed published-package identities.
One immutable public-analyzer release-selection catalog covering alpha.2 and the alpha.3 candidate.
Installed CLI projection of a ready-to-embed public analyzer component.
Defined receipt-generator identity, version, digest, and validation semantics.
Explicit loss-rejecting alpha.1-to-alpha.2 C# gate-definition migration assessment.
One GitHub workflow path using the same package, checksum, selection, and cold-consumer evidence.
Establishment-first private-gate and executable conformance coverage.
nonGoals: No alpha.2 package mutation, repack, deletion, or unlisting.
No package, GitHub Release, deployment, or promotion action under design or implementation authority.
No network lookup during installed CLI selection description.
No new consumer-owned analyzer, Program Kit private diagnostic family, hook, watcher, or autonomous release loop.
No weakening of exact package, assembly, schema, selection-lock, generated-output, or compiler-participation verification.
No promise that a pre-fix alpha.2 source rebuild can reproduce already-published alpha.2 bytes.
No claim that a local builder can reproduce NuGet.org's repository signature or the raw SHA-256 of a repository-signed package.
assumptions: NuGet.org retains the immutable published alpha.2 analyzer nupkg whose SHA-256 is 282a10899e45c302cb0ba879b01f9ff6bf92bee0a73fd5c996ad77a4dee22a6c.
The alpha.2 analyzer assembly SHA-256 is 7ec050ca9434657060b8e18400fc8d2db26424424e1840925abe383c4bc4e8e1.

The historical GitHub alpha.2 handoff analyzer nupkg SHA-256 is 96cf2d7fd2cff80b4d10a00d11e2375318cec3639af89ed451070eb699e6b8b5 and is not authoritative for a NuGet.org consumer binding because it names different bytes.
The exact supported .NET 10.0.302 SDK remains pinned; reproducible package-envelope bytes do not depend on an unreleased SDK or future NuGet capability.

A repository-owned canonical package writer can preserve the SDK-produced entry contents while emitting ordinal entries, a fixed ZIP-compatible timestamp, normalized attributes, and uncompressed payloads reproducibly.

NuGet.org adds or countersigns .signature.p7s after upload; the raw published-package SHA-256 therefore differs from the reproducible unsigned candidate SHA-256 while non-signature entry contents remain equivalent.
A fixed ZIP-compatible package timestamp is reproducibility metadata rather than a claim about human decision time.
The existing Program Kit private C# gate remains the semantic owner of PKCS source diagnostics.
The current manifest-selected source packer is the intended release-package-set authority and may be extended rather than replaced.
The human accepts that analyzer-first publication is not atomic across the complete alpha.3 package set, while implementation and workflow invocation remain separately authorized.

The removal of the unreleased SDK dependency, repository-owned package canonicalization, analyzer-first published-evidence finalization, accepted partial-publication risk, and continued withholding of workflow invocation authority.
The implemented deterministic flags, stable compiler outputs, fresh generated-file root, pinned 10.0.302 SDK, and repository-wide analyzer attachment.
The implemented fresh invocation root, stable receipt representation, nonce transport, path mapping, and participation receipt verification boundary.
The current 29 manifest-selected package projects and roles.
The one-restore, one-build, manifest-selected aggregate pack transaction and current package manifest.
The current divergent workflow that enumerates src directories and separately packs the meta-package.
The analyzer source inputs, package layout, public contract, and compiler-participation generator type without binary or generated-output generator selection evidence.
The current installed describe-definition projection and its non-value package digest evidence text.
The value-preserving but currently non-executable alpha.1-to-alpha.2 migration semantics.
The current package-only proof, including its synthetic analyzer bytes and hand-supplied assembly digest.
The establishment-first extension of the existing private gate, repository-owned canonical-package checks, candidate/published evidence split, and analyzer-first workflow checks.

vocabulary.meaning: One immutable versioned association between a published analyzer nupkg, its analyzer assembly asset, its public contract, and the exact generated-output generator revisions accepted by the gate.
An exact artifact reference such as pkid:generator:program-kit:dotnet-host whose digest is the SHA-256 of an immutable revision descriptor and whose use is proven by generated-output evidence.

domains.purpose: Own compiler and pack inputs whose normalization makes exact Program Kit outputs independently reproducible.

vocabulary.meaning: The complete manifest-selected package set whose nupkg bytes agree across clean builds of the same source and pinned toolchain.
Fresh build-intermediate proof that analyzers ran, excluded from compiled and packaged product bytes.

domains.purpose: Own the canonical package selection, checksums, analyzer selections, reproducibility observations, and publication input set.

vocabulary.meaning: The exact package manifest, nupkg checksums, public-analyzer selection catalog, and repeat-build comparison consumed by the publication workflow.

domains.purpose: Own C# gate definition, selection, migration assessment, compiler participation, and verification mechanics.

vocabulary.meaning: A loss-rejecting check that preserves an alpha.1 definition when it already conforms to alpha.2 and otherwise reports the exact consumer decision that cannot be invented.

domains.purpose: Own isolated package-only evidence that installed Program Kit mechanics are sufficient for a clean consumer.

vocabulary.meaning: A consumer gate rebind using only CLI-emitted Program Kit selection evidence and consumer-owned inputs.

domains.purpose: Own Program Kit command transport, repository integration, and implementation governance.

semanticModels.meaning: The canonical package, assembly, contract, diagnostic, and generated-output generator values for one published analyzer version.
semanticModels.invariants: Exactly one row exists per version; packageSha256 names the exact NuGet.org repository-signed nupkg consumed by the gate; assemblyDigest names the analyzer DLL inside both candidate and published packages; candidatePackageSha256 and packageContentDigest separately bind reproducible producer bytes and signature-independent entry contents; each generator revision digest equals its immutable descriptor bytes; generated-output evidence names a selected revision; placeholder prose is invalid.

semanticModels.meaning: The pinned source and supported SDK, normalized compiler outputs, repository-owned canonical-package profile, selected projects, exact unsigned candidate packages, signature-independent content digests, and published-package evidence for one Program Kit version.
semanticModels.invariants: Random values and absolute roots remain outside product bytes; the SDK-produced unsigned archive is rewritten through one versioned canonical profile with ordinal entry names, the 1980-01-01T00:00:00Z ZIP timestamp, zero external attributes, and stored payloads; every selected candidate package is compared; signatures are rejected from candidate inputs; the meta-package participates in the same selection and mechanism; NuGet.org signatures are verified and excluded only from packageContentDigest comparison.

semanticModels.meaning: The explicit source schema, target schema, canonical input, preservation outcome, and path diagnostics for an alpha.1-to-alpha.2 gate-definition transition.
semanticModels.invariants: The operation invents no artifact kind, project path, package reference, or packability value; a conforming input is preserved and a nonconforming input fails without output.

components.purpose: Carry immutable public-analyzer selection rows derived from exact finalized packages.
components.compatibilityBoundary: Rows are immutable after publication; new package versions add rows.

components.purpose: Emit one canonical ready-to-embed analyzer component from installed release evidence.
components.compatibilityBoundary: Command JSON is versioned and fails on unavailable or inconsistent package versions.

components.purpose: Carry immutable alpha.2 historical and alpha.3 candidate descriptors for pkid:generator:program-kit:dotnet-host.
components.compatibilityBoundary: A descriptor digest is its exact file SHA-256; changed generator semantics require a new version and descriptor.

components.purpose: Enforce PKCC001 and emit the separate deterministic compiler-participation receipt.
components.compatibilityBoundary: The public diagnostic and package asset layout remain immutable per analyzer package version.

components.purpose: Require deterministic generated-output evidence to name a generator revision selected by the analyzer component.
components.compatibilityBoundary: A structurally valid but unobserved or mismatched receiptGeneratorRevisions entry fails verification.

components.purpose: Build the exact manifest-selected release package closure and rewrite each unsigned SDK-produced archive through the repository-owned canonical package profile.
components.compatibilityBoundary: The repository manifest, pinned 10.0.302 SDK, canonicalization descriptor, and canonical-writer implementation jointly define candidate package bytes; any change requires new evidence and renewed approval.

components.purpose: Verify NuGet.org repository signatures, compare every non-signature entry with the canonical candidate, derive the exact published-package SHA-256, and finalize the alpha.3 analyzer selection before the CLI package is packed.
components.compatibilityBoundary: Only the exact configured NuGet.org service index and announced repository-signing certificates are accepted; a mismatched existing package or changed non-signature entry stops the workflow.

components.purpose: Assess and canonically preserve an alpha.1 gate definition under alpha.2 semantics without inventing consumer facts.
components.compatibilityBoundary: Only explicitly registered schema transitions are accepted.

packages.compatibilityBoundary: The installed tool includes the immutable release-selection catalog used by the read projection.
The analyzer assembly, package layout, public diagnostic, and selected generated-output generator revisions are immutable per package version.
Generator-revision descriptor bytes and their exact source inventories are immutable per revision.
Generator-revision evidence matching remains fail-closed and versioned with build mechanics.

referenceRules.referencedScope: Only exact NuGet.org repository-signed packages whose non-signature contents match a canonical manifest-selected candidate.
referenceRules.rationale: The consumer-facing packageSha256 must derive from the repository-signed bytes the consumer downloads; candidatePackageSha256 and packageContentDigest preserve the reproducible producer and content identities without pretending to reproduce NuGet.org's signature.

referenceRules.referencedScope: The canonical manifest-selected consumer-feed packer and its exact evidence outputs.
referenceRules.rationale: A second project enumeration, separate meta-package packer, or uncanonicalized upload would recreate release-path divergence.

referenceRules.referencingScope: The human-started NuGet GitHub workflow after analyzer-first publication.
referenceRules.referencedScope: The exact repository-signed analyzer download, its verified candidate-content equivalence, and the transaction-local final alpha.3 selection catalog used to pack the CLI.
referenceRules.rationale: NuGet.org's repository signature and raw published digest exist only after upload. Analyzer-first publication is therefore the explicit phase boundary for finalizing an alpha.3 catalog shipped by the same-version CLI.

artifactDecisions.requestedOutcome: Represent canonical public-analyzer selection, deterministic compiler and package production, migration assessment, release convergence, and the consumer proof as one exact review authority.

executableBehavior.rationale: The design grants no build, implementation, publication, workflow, or external mutation authority.

valueLifecycle.rationale: The canonical JSON is schema-validated and digest-bound by the implementation plan and review manifest.

agentRetrieval.rationale: The review set is explicit repository-owned input and creates no retrieval integration.

agentProcedure.rationale: This artifact creates no capability, hook, watcher, MCP binding, tool binding, or autonomous procedure.

humanCommunication.audience: The human Program Kit reviewer and later bounded implementer.
humanCommunication.decisionAuthorityBoundary: Only explicit human approval of the exact design and plan digests authorizes implementation; publication remains separately withheld.
humanCommunication.rationale: The design, gate amendment, plan, validation report, and manifest expose exact boundaries, proof obligations, risks, and stop conditions.

governance.provenancePolicy: The original and amendment human inputs, current Program Kit source commit a3c2fe174cd3511e9f3787acb4f7fd2ef59dba07, implemented W010/W020 evidence, and exact observed artifact hashes are named.
governance.digestPolicy: Material change requires schema revalidation, new exact digests, and renewed human approval.
governance.compatibilityPolicy: Published package rows and alpha.2 bytes remain immutable; commands, schemas, and release evidence version explicitly.
governance.migrationPolicy: Gate definitions use explicit registered transitions; package versions add immutable selection rows and are never overwritten.

dataHandling.redactionPolicy: Artifacts contain repository paths, identities, versions, digests, commands, and outcomes only.
dataHandling.externalizationPolicy: Only separately approved GitHub and NuGet workflows may externalize release evidence and package bytes.
dataHandling.ephemeralDataPolicy: Temporary roots, compiler nonces, process observations, and credentials are excluded from durable design content.

artifactDecisions.rationale: A schema-governed amendment is required because the accepted alpha.3 consumer journey did not define canonical analyzer binary selections, prove inner package reproducibility, distinguish unsigned candidate bytes from NuGet.org repository-signed bytes, or account for the publication-time finalization needed by a same-version installed CLI.

security.policy: Fresh compiler participation is proven from one prepared contained invocation root; caller-authored or stale receipts fail.
guarantees: Selected analyzer assemblies are checked by exact digest.
The receipt generator remains in the selected analyzer assembly.
Random nonces are excluded from product bytes.
NuGet.org repository signatures are verified before their raw package digest becomes consumer selection authority.
Signature-independent package-content comparison rejects any repository-side payload change.
exclusions: The design does not prove compiler or NuGet service freedom from defects.

authority.policy: Design approval, implementation approval, package version selection, and publication are separate human decisions.
guarantees: The CLI selection command is read-only and non-authoritative.
The GitHub workflow cannot be invoked by implementation work.
exclusions: No principal, decision time, release approval, or publication success is inferred.

secrets.policy: Build and proof artifacts contain no NuGet credentials, OIDC tokens, or secret values.
guarantees: Temporary publication credentials remain workflow-owned.
exclusions: The design does not inspect or manage repository secrets.

persistence.policy: Canonical release evidence is immutable per package version and transaction-local output is promoted atomically.
guarantees: Existing output roots are refused.
Alpha.2 remains unchanged and listed.
A changed candidate byte invalidates prior evidence.
exclusions: Temporary build directories are not durable evidence.

failure.policy: Missing, duplicate, placeholder, non-reproducible, mismatched, unsigned-published, content-divergent, or unknown selections fail closed; after analyzer-first publication a later failure leaves explicit partial-release evidence and publishes no remaining package.
guarantees: Migration assessment emits no partial target.
CLI selection emits no row for an unregistered version.
The analyzer-first workflow phase follows complete candidate evidence.
Remaining package publication follows repository-signature verification, candidate-content equivalence, final alpha.3 catalog materialization, repeat-pack equality, and cold-consumer verification.
exclusions: External service outages are reported but not repaired automatically.

concurrency.policy: Bounded aggregate packing may run concurrently only after one exact build and with isolated transaction paths.
guarantees: Parallel order does not affect package or manifest bytes.
exclusions: Concurrent publication of the same version is not supported.

cancellation.policy: Cancellation before the first push publishes nothing. Cancellation after analyzer-first publication may leave that immutable analyzer version present; a retry resumes only after verifying its exact published bytes and candidate-content equivalence.
guarantees: Staging output is not promoted after cancellation or failure.
No retry overwrites, repacks, or silently accepts an existing published package.
A mismatched existing analyzer version stops instead of continuing.
exclusions: Cleanup does not delete consumer or previously promoted output.
NuGet.org does not provide atomic multi-package publication or rollback; the accepted analyzer-first phase boundary is explicit.

observability.policy: Evidence records source commit, pinned SDK, canonicalization profile, package set, candidate package SHA-256, signature-independent package-content digest, published package SHA-256, repository-signature verification, comparison results, and cold-proof outcomes.
guarantees: Absolute temporary roots and credentials are excluded.
Each published analyzer row identifies exact NuGet.org-signed package and analyzer assembly bytes.
Candidate and published evidence are linked without asserting that a local builder reproduces NuGet.org's signature.
exclusions: Logs are not authority or a substitute for canonical evidence.

compatibility.policy: Published versions are immutable; new command and evidence contracts add explicit alpha revisions while legacy readers remain.
guarantees: Alpha.2 remains available for restore and rollback.
Alpha.3 never overwrites alpha.2.
The migration assessment preserves already-conforming alpha.1 gate bytes.
exclusions: Reproducing the historical alpha.2 source build is not guaranteed.

scenarios.actor: A consumer with only the installed alpha.3 Program Kit CLI and public NuGet access.
scenarios.intent: Rebind a consumer-owned gate from the alpha.1 analyzer selection to the immutable alpha.2 or alpha.3 public analyzer.
preconditions: The requested analyzer version is present in the installed release-selection catalog.
The consumer owns the gate definition, lock intent, and repository paths.
steps: Invoke describe-public-analyzer-selection for the exact package version.
Embed the emitted canonical analyzer component without supplying Program Kit-internal digests.
Assess or materialize the gate definition under alpha.2 semantics.
outcomes: The definition binds the exact immutable nupkg and analyzer assembly.
The dotnet-host generator has one exact versioned descriptor whose digest is execution-linked through generated-output evidence.
Verification completes without a Program Kit checkout.
failureOutcomes: An unavailable version, mismatched digest, nonconforming alpha.1 artifact selection, or tampered package fails with no output.

scenarios.actor: A Program Kit contributor or GitHub Actions runner using the pinned source and SDK.
scenarios.intent: Produce the exact alpha.3 candidate package and evidence set independently.
preconditions: The clean source commit and pinned SDK are identical.
The output roots do not exist.
steps: Restore and build once with stable generated sources and normalized paths.
Pack the manifest-selected complete package set with the pinned supported SDK.
Reject signatures and unsafe or duplicate paths, then rewrite every unsigned archive through the versioned repository canonicalization profile.
Repeat from a second clean absolute root.
Compare every assembly, portable PDB, candidate nupkg, package-content digest, package manifest, and checksum projection.
outcomes: Every selected unsigned candidate nupkg is byte-identical without an unreleased SDK.
The analyzer candidate evidence binds its exact package-content and assembly digests without pretending to know NuGet.org-signed bytes.
Only the exact evidence-backed package set becomes eligible for publication.
failureOutcomes: Any differing package, signature-bearing candidate, unsafe or duplicate entry, extra or missing project, content drift, path leak, or placeholder selection blocks the candidate.

scenarios.actor: The human Program Kit release authority.
scenarios.intent: Start the bounded analyzer-first alpha.3 publication workflow after implementation and candidate evidence are complete, allowing the workflow to derive NuGet.org-signed selection evidence before packing the CLI.
preconditions: The exact implementation plan was approved and completed.
The branch is merged and the deterministic candidate and workflow-conformance evidence passed.
The agent has explicitly handed off the GitHub workflow action.
steps: Review the final commit, canonicalization profile, candidate evidence, workflow phases, and accepted partial-publication boundary.
Create or confirm the exact v0.1.0-alpha.3 tag as required by the workflow.
Run the approved GitHub NuGet publication workflow.

The workflow publishes or verifies the exact analyzer candidate, downloads and verifies its NuGet.org repository-signed bytes, finalizes the alpha.3 selection catalog, repeat-packs and cold-verifies the CLI and complete remaining closure, then publishes the remaining packages.
A safe retry verifies an already-published analyzer before resuming and never overwrites it.
outcomes: The installed alpha.3 CLI emits the exact NuGet.org-signed analyzer package SHA-256, assembly digest, and generator revision.
GitHub Release evidence records both reproducible unsigned candidates and repository-signed published packages with signature-independent content equivalence.
failureOutcomes: A tag/version mismatch, failed candidate qualification, repository-signature failure, content mismatch, changed existing package, or cold-proof failure stops the workflow.
A failure after analyzer-first publication leaves explicit immutable partial-release evidence; it does not roll back or silently publish remaining packages.

statusClaims.claim: The amended review design exists from explicit human intent and current repository source truth. PKRB-W010 and PKRB-W020 are implemented and evidence-bound; controlled package canonicalization, published-evidence finalization, remaining product work, and publication are not claimed.

Compiler-output reproducibility is implemented. Canonical unsigned package bytes, repository-signed published evidence, same-version catalog finalization, and workflow resumption behavior remain blocked pending exact amendment approval and implementation.
